claims.statement: For events Xi with marginals pi, max(0, sum_i pi - (m-1)) <= P(intersection_i Xi) <= min_i pi, with both bounds attainable; pi alone does not imply the product bound.
assumptions: Xi are events on one probability space
only the marginal probabilities are supplied for the bound
claims.status: internally reconstructed; standard Frechet coupling result
claims.novelty_boundary: No novelty claim for the probability inequality; application is a scoped audit of guide-level resistance inference.
costs: Joint escape and function require phased haplotype and functional assays
Population-level costs and dynamics are outside the theorem
claims.falsifier: The coupling theorem is falsified only by an error in the mathematical statement/proof; the biological independence premise is falsified by same-haplotype co-occurrence beyond the product prediction or a common multi-target deletion.
claims.next_gate: Measure guide-level marginals, same-haplotype all-site escape, and functional escape on independent germline-origin transmissions; report effective sample size and assay dropout.

claims.statement: A per-guide marginal panel alone cannot certify exponential suppression of functional resistance; for F subset of complete molecular escape B, P(F) <= min_i pi, and functional retention within B needs a target-specific assay/model.
assumptions: Xi encode all guide-site states relevant to cleavage escape
all functional guide-resistant alleles lie in B; unobserved structural routes require an added bound s
claims.status: conditional theorem plus principled rejection of marginal-only inference
claims.novelty_boundary: Prior work already documents structural deletions and function-preserving resistance; this is not claimed as a new biological mechanism.
claims.falsifier: For a proposed design, a functional escape class not represented in the measured molecular escape state falsifies the assay completeness assumption; measured P(F) above the preregistered ceiling rejects that design guarantee.
claims.next_gate: Pre-register epsilon and assay detection limits; acquire transmission-level observations and functionally classify recurrent escape haplotypes.
